affordance_in_statement: The Hauler drone follows the Scout along the exact same sequence of checkpoints. ... it can only begin its extraction at a checkpoint after the Scout has completely finished its inspection at that same checkpoint. removal_suggestion: Replace the exact-same-sequence requirement with a rule that lets the Hauler choose its own checkpoint order independently, while retaining the existing input and output formats.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes and directly applies Johnson's rule: p1 <= p2 jobs first in increasing p1, followed by p1 > p2 jobs in decreasing p2.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The Hauler drone follows the Scout along the exact same sequence of checkpoints, with the Hauler waiting for Scout completion and serializing its own extractions.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the identical Johnson partition and ordering, then computes the standard two-machine flow-shop makespan.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The Hauler drone follows the Scout along the exact same sequence of checkpoints, with one extraction at a time and release after the Scout's inspection.

common_affordance: The two drones form a two-machine permutation flow shop: every checkpoint must use the same order on Scout and Hauler, and Hauler processing is serialized after Scout release.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Sorts every checkpoint by p2 descending, which is not Johnson's ordering and ignores the required p1 <= p2 / p1 > p2 partition.
Assumes sorting by p1 descending is optimal; this reverses the relevant Johnson ordering and does not account for p2-based ordering in the second group.

recommended_edit: Change "The Hauler drone follows the Scout along the exact same sequence of checkpoints" to "The Hauler drone may choose and follow its own sequence of checkpoints independently of the Scout." This removes the permutation-flow-shop assumption without changing the input, output, bounds, tie-breaks, or example values.
